evals.prompt: We're a building supplies retailer. Right now anyone can see our prices online, but we want to hide them behind a 'sign in to see trade price' gate for verified trade accounts only. Help me design that screen.
evals.expected_output: Should check for marketing-strategy.md first. Should identify this as a trade/wholesale price gate trigger. Should apply the gate screen components: headline focused on what unlocking gets them, a value preview (price range or savings %), a fast verify/sign-in path, a trust signal, a specific CTA, and an escape hatch to continue as a retail customer. Should provide specific copy recommendations. Should NOT recommend building a paid membership/points program (that's loyalty's territory).
assertions: Checks for marketing-strategy.md
Identifies as trade/wholesale price gate
Applies gate screen components framework
Includes headline, value preview, unlock action, trust signal, CTA
Includes escape hatch to standard/retail price
Provides specific copy recommendations
Does not conflate this with a paid loyalty program

evals.prompt: In our cart, we want to show customers that if they add more units they'll unlock a cheaper price per unit. How should that work?
evals.expected_output: Should identify this as a quantity/bulk-break unlock trigger. Should recommend showing the current tier and the next tier live in cart, updating as quantity changes, with clear math (e.g. 'add 3 more to unlock $X/unit') rather than requiring the buyer to calculate it themselves. Should reference the quantity break unlock example format. Should not treat this as a full re-gate requiring a separate unlock action.
assertions: Identifies as quantity/bulk-break unlock trigger
Recommends showing current and next tier live in cart
Recommends clear 'add X more to unlock' framing
Does not require a separate registration/unlock step
References the cart-level example pattern

evals.prompt: We want our Black Friday sale to open to registered members 24 hours before everyone else. This isn't a paid program, just free sign-up for early access. How do we design the gate?
evals.expected_output: Should identify this as a members-only early access gate, explicitly distinct from a paid loyalty/rewards program (should reference loyalty and clarify the difference). Should recommend previewing what's coming without giving away full details, being explicit about when it opens to everyone, and applying the gate screen components. Should recommend an escape hatch (e.g. 'remind me when it opens to everyone').
assertions: Identifies as members-only early access gate
Explicitly distinguishes this from a paid loyalty program and references loyalty
Recommends a teaser/preview before the full reveal
Recommends stating clearly when it opens to everyone
Includes an escape hatch option

evals.prompt: An item is out of stock. We want to let people enter their email to get notified when it's back, but I've heard we need to be careful about consent if we also want to market to them later.
evals.expected_output: Should identify this as a restock/waitlist gate. Should recommend a simple single-field unlock (email) and confirming what happens next. Should flag the compliance point directly: a one-time restock notification tied to that product is not the same as ongoing marketing consent, and if the retailer wants to also send marketing, that requires separate clear consent under Spam Act 2003 (AU) / Unsolicited Electronic Messages Act 2007 (NZ) or equivalent (CAN-SPAM, PECR, ePrivacy). Should reference compliance.
assertions: Identifies as restock/waitlist gate
Recommends simple single-field (email) unlock
Distinguishes one-time restock notification from ongoing marketing consent
Cites AU/NZ consent regulations first, with US/UK/EU as secondary reference
References the compliance skill

evals.prompt: What are common mistakes retailers make with these kinds of gated-access screens? We don't want to trick customers or get in trouble.
evals.expected_output: Should apply the anti-patterns section. Should cover dark patterns (inflating the 'standard' price to make the gated price look better, fake or non-resetting scarcity/countdowns, requiring full account creation for something that only needs an email) and conversion killers (gating content that didn't need gating, repeated re-prompting, hard-to-find escape hatch). Should flag that false scarcity/urgency claims can trigger regulatory action (ACCC/Ad Standards, Commerce Commission/ASA, FTC) and reference compliance.
assertions: Applies anti-patterns section
Covers dark patterns specific to retail gates (inflated standard price, fake scarcity, unnecessary account creation)
Covers conversion killers
Flags regulatory risk of false scarcity/urgency claims
References the compliance skill

evals.prompt: We want to launch a paid VIP membership program where customers pay $99/year for free shipping, early access, and bonus points on every purchase. Can you help design this?
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this is the design of an ongoing paid membership/rewards program, not a one-time gate/unlock screen, and defer to or cross-reference the loyalty skill instead of attempting to design it within paywalls. Should explain the distinction: paywalls covers the interaction design of a gate moment (price reveal, early-access unlock, restock alert), while loyalty covers the structure of the program itself (tiers, points, paid membership benefits).
assertions: Recognizes this as ongoing paid membership/rewards program design, not a gate screen
Defers to or references the loyalty skill
Explains the distinction between paywalls (gate moments) and loyalty (program design)
Does not attempt to design the membership program within paywalls
